text: In the first year that Cyrus ruled over Persia, the LORD moved Cyrus to act so that the promise spoken through Jeremiah would come true, and Cyrus put out a written order across his whole realm, saying:
This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: The LORD, the God of the heavens, has given me every kingdom on earth, and he has appointed me to build him a house at Jerusalem, in Judah.
Any of his people among you — may his God be with him — may go up to Jerusalem in Judah and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel, the God who is there.
And every survivor, in whatever place he lives, is to be helped by the local people with silver, gold, goods, and animals, along with a freewill gift for the house of God in Jerusalem.
So the family heads of Judah and Benjamin, along with the priests and Levites — everyone whose heart God had moved — got ready to go up and build the LORD's house in Jerusalem.
All their neighbors supported them with silver articles, gold, goods, animals, and valuable gifts, in addition to whatever was given freely.
King Cyrus also brought out the articles belonging to the LORD's house that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem and placed in the house of his own god.
Cyrus king of Persia had them brought out by Mithredath the treasurer, who counted them out to Sheshbazzar, the leader of Judah.
This was the count: thirty gold dishes, a thousand silver dishes, twenty-nine silver pans,
thirty gold bowls, four hundred ten silver bowls of a lesser kind, and a thousand other articles.
In all there were five thousand four hundred articles of gold and silver, and Sheshbazzar brought all of them along when the exiles were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.
